html:
The Diaguita are an Indigenous people of the Norte Chico of Chile and the northwest of Argentina, in the valleys of La Rioja, Catamarca, Salta and Tucumán. They were never one state but many valley chiefdoms who spoke the Cacán language.

They farmed maize, beans and squash on irrigated terraces, herded llamas, and made fine painted pottery and bronze work. In the late 1400s the Inca Empire conquered them and moved some to other parts of its realm. After the Spanish came, the Diaguita of the Calchaquí valleys fought them in the Calchaquí Wars, which went on, with long pauses, from 1560 to 1667. In the end the Spanish broke them up and deported many, including the Quilmes, who were marched to near Buenos Aires. Their neighbours included the Omaguaca to the north and the Comechingones to the southeast.
